Running any fuel-burning device in an enclosed space can produce carbon monoxide (CO), which is an invisible and odorless gas that can lead to CO poisoning. CO poisoning has symptoms similar to those of the flu, including headache, dizziness, nausea, weakness, confusion, blurred vision, and fatigue. The risk is especially high when multiple people or pets are in the same enclosed space. Symptoms may not be immediately obvious, and victims often do not recognize what is happening until it's too late. To prevent CO poisoning, you should run any camp stove outdoors, or only with a wide cross-draft to ensure proper ventilation. Additionally, placing a battery-powered carbon monoxide alarm in your shelter will help alert you if levels of CO become unsafe.

The Rule of 3s is a guideline used in survival situations to prioritize what needs immediate attention. It states:

• ~3 MINUTES without AIR — or with an uncontrolled airway / severe bleeding.
• ~3 HOURS without SHELTER in harsh weather — exposure (hypothermia or heat) kills faster than thirst and is the #1 wilderness killer.
• ~3 DAYS without WATER.
• ~3 WEEKS without FOOD.

This prioritization helps ensure that life-threatening issues are addressed first, before other needs such as shelter, water, and food.
